extracted.intended_audience: Authors preparing manuscripts of observational (cohort, case–control, cross-sectional) epidemiological studies; journal editors and reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing clear, transparent manuscripts reporting observational epidemiological studies (cohort, case–control, cross-sectional) using the 22-item STROBE checklist to enable critical appraisal and indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract (Item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate the study’s design with a commonly used term in the title or the abstract; provide in the abstract an informative and balanced summary of what was done and what was found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the adopted study design in the manuscript title to ensure correct indexing and visibility; abstracts should summarise only information present in the manuscript body and be informative and balanced to improve discoverability and citation potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background / Rationale (Item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the scientific background and rationale for the investigation being reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The introduction should set the scene for the study by providing relevant background information that motivates the research question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives (Item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: State specific objectives, including any prespecified hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly articulate study aims and any a priori hypotheses so readers can evaluate whether analyses and interpretations address stated objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design (Item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present key elements of study design early in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the actual methodology rather than using shorthand labels such as 'prospective', 'retrospective', 'concurrent', or 'historical'; early clarity about design enables critical appraisal of methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting (Item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the setting, locations, and relevant dates, including periods of recruitment, exposure, follow-up, and data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting where and when the study occurred (including recruitment and follow-up periods) helps readers assess context and temporal applicability of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants (Item 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohort: eligibility criteria, sources and methods of selection, methods of follow-up; Case–control: eligibility criteria, case ascertainment and control selection, rationale for choices; Cross-sectional: eligibility criteria and sources/methods of participant selection. For matched studies give matching criteria and numbers (exposed/unexposed or controls per case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor participant reporting to the design: explain inclusion/exclusion, recruitment procedures, ascertainment methods, matching criteria and counts. This enables assessment of selection bias and generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variables (Item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define all outcomes, exposures, predictors, potential confounders, and effect modifiers; give diagnostic criteria, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide operational definitions and diagnostic criteria so readers can understand what was measured and how key variables were defined, facilitating reproducibility and validity assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources / Measurement (Item 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each variable of interest, give sources of data and details of methods of assessment (measurement); describe comparability of assessment methods if there is more than one group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report measurement tools, instruments, and procedures for each variable and note if different groups had different assessment methods; where applicable give information separately for cases and controls or for exposed and unexposed groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias (Item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any efforts to address potential sources of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe strategies used to identify, reduce, or assess bias (selection, information, confounding), so readers can judge credibility of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study size (Item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the study size was arrived at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sample size determination, power considerations, or rationale for chosen size, and include confidence intervals considered to show whether statistical precision was adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative variables (Item 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how quantitative variables were handled in the analyses; if applicable, describe which groupings were chosen and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether variables were analysed continuously or categorised, justify any cut-points, and describe transformations so readers can assess potential information loss or bias from categorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods (Item 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe all statistical methods, including those used to control for confounding; describe any methods used to examine subgroups and interactions; explain how missing data were addressed. Design-specific: Cohort—explain how loss to follow-up was addressed; Case–control—explain how matching was addressed; Cross-sectional—describe analytical methods taking account of sampling strategy. Describe any sensitivity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full details of analytic approaches, adjustment strategies, subgroup and interaction analyses, handling of missing data (imputation, exclusions), and sensitivity analyses to enable replication and assessment of analytical robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants — numbers at each stage (Item 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report numbers of individuals at each stage of study (e.g., potentially eligible, examined for eligibility, confirmed eligible, included, completing follow-up, analyzed); give reasons for nonparticipation at each stage; consider use of a flow diagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a transparent accounting of participant flow with counts and reasons for exclusions/nonparticipation; flow diagrams are encouraged to summarise stages clearly. Give information separately for cases/controls or exposed/unexposed when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive data (Item 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give characteristics of study participants (e.g., demographic, clinical, social) and information on exposures and potential confounders; indicate number of participants with missing data for each variable of interest; Cohort—summarize follow-up time (e.g., average and total amount).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report baseline/descriptive characteristics and missingness to help assess representativeness and potential confounding; where relevant provide follow-up time metrics for cohort studies. Give information separately for relevant groups when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome data (Item 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohort—report numbers of outcome events or summary measures over time; Case–control—report numbers in each exposure category or summary measures of exposure; Cross-sectional—report numbers of outcome events or summary measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present outcome data appropriate to the design to allow readers to understand event counts, exposure distributions, and timing; give group-specific details when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main results (Item 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give unadjusted estimates and, if applicable, confounder-adjusted estimates and their precision (e.g., 95% CI); make clear which confounders were adjusted for and why; report category boundaries when continuous variables were categorized; if relevant, consider translating relative risks into absolute risk for a meaningful time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both crude and adjusted measures with confidence intervals, justify adjustment variables, and make results interpretable (e.g., absolute risks) to aid clinical or public-health relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other analyses (Item 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report other analyses done (e.g., analyses of subgroups and interactions, and sensitivity analyses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present secondary, subgroup, interaction, and sensitivity analyses transparently, indicating whether they were prespecified or exploratory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key results (Item 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize key results with reference to study objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin the discussion by directly relating main findings back to the original objectives and hypotheses to frame interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations (Item 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss limitations of the study, taking into account sources of potential bias or imprecision; discuss both direction and magnitude of any potential bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an objective assessment of study weaknesses, including likely direction and size of biases and how they might affect conclusions; avoid overinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation (Item 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a cautious overall interpretation of results considering objectives, limitations, multiplicity of analyses, results from similar studies, and other relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize findings within existing literature and methodological constraints, acknowledging uncertainty and avoiding causal claims when unjustified by design (e.g., non-longitudinal studies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability (Item 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the generalizability (external validity) of the study results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address to whom and under what circumstances the results may apply, considering setting, population, and study procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding (Item 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the source of funding and the role of the funders for the present study and, if applicable, for the original study on which the present article is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report funding sources and describe the funders' roles (if any) in study design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, and manuscript preparation; include conflicts of interest for authors and funders.
